test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Sept, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Two trains are travelling in the same direction on parallel tracks. Train A is travelling at 30 km/h and Train B is travelling at 60 km/h. If Train A is 400 m long and it takes Train B two minutes to pass Train A, what is the length of Train B?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Same direction) = 60 − 30 = 30 km/h.

30 km/h in m/s = 30 × (5/18) = 25/3 m/s.

**Total Distance** (Length of A + B) = Speed × Time = (25/3) × 120 = 1000 m.

Length of Train B = 1000 − 400 = 600 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d1cd345f08a6f6a8d98b4efc25820205162b7afa0a4f139e92d3add6651ded7.png] 

**Given:** Speed of Train A = 30 km/h, Speed of Train B = 60 km/h, Length of Train A = 400 m, Time = 2 minutes = 120 seconds.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ **Relative Speed** = 60 − 30 = 30 km/h

⇒ Conversion to m/s = 30 × (5/18) = 25/3 m/s

⇒ Let length of Train B be **LB**

⇒ Total Distance = LA + LB = 400 + LB

⇒ 400 + LB = (25/3) × 120

⇒ 400 + LB = 25 × 40

⇒ 400 + LB = 1000

⇒ LB = 1000 − 400 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂). In the **opposite direction**, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Rule

When one train passes another, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum of the lengths** of both trains (L₁ + L₂).</p
